$comment: Exceptions to the advisory gate (scripts/check-audit.mjs). Any advisory npm audit reports at `moderate` or above fails CI, whether the affected package is a production or a development dependency: there is one threshold and one mechanism, and no tier that quietly does not block. An exception is never silent — it is an entry below, with a written `reason`, and it is BOUND to the finding it excuses. `advisory` is the identity: the GHSA identifier from the advisory URL, or the numeric `source` when npm reports no GHSA. `package`, `severity` and `range` must equal what npm audit reports today, compared exactly; if any of them moves — the advisory re-pointed at another package, the severity changed in either direction, the vulnerable range widened or narrowed — the entry no longer describes the finding and the gate FAILS rather than inheriting the old reason. An entry whose advisory has dropped below the threshold is to be deleted, not re-bound, and fails until it is. An entry naming an advisory this audit does not report at all fails too, so a stale excuse cannot sit here waiting to cover a finding nobody decided. Adding an entry is a decision about risk, not a build fix. The same shape guards `contrast-known-failures.json` in kodera-hq/kodera-design-tokens. Every accepted entry also requires an installed array with the complete exact path/version/resolved-source/SHA-512-integrity set. The checker unions all matching advisory occurrences before comparing that set to package-lock.json; missing, extra or drifting nodes/provenance refuse the exception.
